<submission>
**Problem summary:** A 52-year-old man with one year of chronic watery diarrhoea, weight loss, distal numbness, and six months of exertional breathlessness and fatigue has findings raising possible systemic amyloidosis with cardiac and neuropathic involvement.

**Working differential:** The symptom cluster — chronic watery diarrhoea, distal numbness, significant weight loss, and new heart-failure symptoms — together with echocardiographic symmetric left-ventricular wall thickening (septum 14.1 mm), reduced LVEF 36%, grade-II diastolic dysfunction, and relative apical sparing on strain, strongly raises suspicion of infiltrative cardiomyopathy, particularly amyloidosis, with autonomic/neuropathic gastrointestinal involvement. Historical laboratory values (NT-proBNP 887 pg/mL, hs-troponin T 23.9 ng/L, creatinine 1.3 mg/dL, eGFR 62.7) support cardiac strain and mild renal impairment at initial assessment, but are not current values; updated vitals and bloods are unreported and must not be assumed.

**What investigations establish and do not:** Negative serum/urine immunofixation and free-light-chain testing argue against AL amyloidosis but do not exclude it entirely, nor do they address ATTR. The sessile serrated lesion with dysplasia explains a colonic lesion but not the systemic picture. No TTR genetic or tissue amyloid results are available; none should be assumed.

**Priorities before final aetiology:** Confirm tissue amyloid typing if biopsy is pursued, clarify TTR genetic status, repeat current cardiac and renal markers, and characterise the neuropathy and diarrhoea mechanism.
</submission>
